title: NCBI Submission Protocol for Microbial Pathogen Surveillance
author: Candace Hope Bias
materials: Release date : Choose "Release immediately following processing".

steps.title: Set up NCBI User Account
steps.instruction: Create an individual user account at NCBI.

substeps.instruction: Visit https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/account
Use the signup link at the bottom of the page
Choose the signup option appropriate for your institution

steps.title: Establish NCBI Submission User Group
steps.instruction: Create or join a submission user group to ensure consistent data ownership and allow multiple staff members to manage submissions.

substeps.instruction: Sign into your personal NCBI account and check the 'Group' tab in the Submission Portal (https://submit.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/groups/) to see if a group already exists.

To create a new group, go to the profile page (https://submit.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/accounts/profile/), scroll to the bottom, and click 'Create group for shared submissions' (ensure all required profile fields marked with '*' are filled first).
Enter the required short name, full name, and contact information.
Invite members via the 'Invite members' button or 'Invites' tab by adding their email addresses.

steps.title: Manage User Group Permissions
steps.instruction: Maintain the user group membership and assign appropriate permission levels.

substeps.instruction: Access the group via the 'group' tab in the submission portal and clicking the Group Id hyperlink.
Assign permissions: READ (view only), MODIFY/SUBMIT/DELETE (submit or retract data), or ADMIN (invite/remove members).
Ensure at least one member has ADMIN privileges.

steps.title: Bookmark Submission Portal
steps.instruction: Bookmark the 'My submissions' page (https://submit.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/subs/) to track current and past submissions.

steps.title: Identify or Establish BioProjects
steps.instruction: Determine if a BioProject (Umbrella or Data) exists or needs to be created.

substeps.instruction: If part of a surveillance network (e.g., GenomeTrakr, NARMS, Vet-LIRN, NAHLN, PulseNet), follow the network coordinator's guidance.
For GenomeTrakr: link a new data project to an established umbrella BioProject. Use PRJNA593772 for taxonomic classification or PRJNA706684 for multi-species/non-targeted projects.

Reference GenomeTrakr Umbrella projects: Campylobacter sp. (PRJNA258021), Cronobacter sp. (PRJNA258402), E. coli/Shigella (PRJNA230919), Listeria sp. (PRJNA514048), Salmonella sp. (PRJNA183844), Vibrio sp. (PRJNA245885), All others (PRJNA706684).
If no data BioProject exists, create one following the 'Create a new BioProject' steps.

steps.title: Create a New Data BioProject
steps.instruction: Establish a data BioProject linked to an existing umbrella BioProject.

substeps.instruction: Navigate to https://submit.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/subs/, click 'BioProject' in the 'Start a new submission' box, and click 'New submission'.
SUBMITTER tab: Select the submission group and describe the organization/laboratory.
PROJECT TYPE tab: Set Project data type to 'Genome sequencing and assembly' and Sample scope to 'multi-species'.
TARGET tab: For targeted pathogens, enter the Genus name (e.g., Salmonella sp.); for non-targeted, enter 'bacteria'. Provide a project scope description (e.g., 'enteric bacteria').

GENERAL INFO tab: Select 'Release immediately following processing', provide a title (e.g., 'GenomeTrakr Project: NY State Dept. of Health, Wadsworth Center'), a public description, and set relevance to 'environmental'.
Link to Umbrella: Select 'Yes' for 'Is your project part of a larger initiative', provide a brief description and the umbrella BioProject accession number.
BIOSAMPLE tab: Leave blank.
PUBLICATIONS tab: Include relevant laboratory publications if applicable.
REVIEW & SUBMIT tab: Review and click 'submit'.
Retrieve the accession number (PRJNAxxxxxx) from the 'My Submissions' page or email.
If part of a coordinated effort (e.g., GenomeTrakr), alert the coordinating body (e.g., genometrakr@fda.hhs.gov).

steps.title: Create a New Umbrella BioProject
steps.instruction: Establish an umbrella BioProject to group multiple data BioProjects.

substeps.instruction: Follow the 'Create a New Data BioProject' steps with these modifications:
PROJECT TYPE tab: Select 'multi-species'.
TARGET tab: Leave Organism name blank; provide a list/description of species (e.g., 'bacterial foodborne pathogens').
GENERAL INFO tab: Provide an Umbrella BioProject Title and select 'NO' for 'Is your project part of a larger initiative'.
Finalization: Email bioprojecthelp@ncbi.nlm.nih.gov requesting conversion of the PRJNA##### to an Umbrella BioProject, specifying the effort (e.g., SARS-CoV-2, GenomeTrakr).

steps.title: Perform Pre-Submission Quality Control
steps.instruction: Verify that sequence data meet the quality control (QC) thresholds of the surveillance network.

substeps.instruction: If not completed, use the GalaxyTrakr MicroRunQC workflow by Ruth Timme for quality control assessment.

steps.title: Submit Data to NCBI
steps.instruction: Submit sample metadata, SRA metadata, and raw sequence data compliant with the Pathogen DOM data structure.

substeps.instruction: Organize submissions so each workflow is dedicated to a single BioProject; initiate distinct submissions for multiple BioProjects.
Navigate to https://submit.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/subs/ and click 'Sequence Read Archive' to start a submission, then click 'New submission'.
SUBMITTER tab: Select the submission group and describe the organization/laboratory; click 'Continue'.

GENERAL INFO tab: Select 'Yes' for BioProject and paste the data BioProject accession (e.g., PRJNA614995). Select 'NO' for BioSample. Set release date to 'Release immediately following processing'. Click 'Continue'.
BIOSAMPLE TYPE tab: Choose the appropriate metadata package (e.g., 'One Health Enteric' for GenomeTrakr).

BIOSAMPLE ATTRIBUTES tab: Select 'Upload a file using Excel or text format (tab-delimited)', upload the populated metadata template, provide antibiogram data if available, and click 'Continue'. Resolve red errors; review yellow warnings.
SRA METADATA tab: Select 'Upload a file using Excel or text format (tab-delimited)', upload the SRA metadata template, and click 'Continue'. Resolve red errors; review yellow warnings.
FILES tab: Select the transfer method (Web browser for ~48 sequences, or FTP/Aspera for stability). Do not check 'Autofinish submission'.
REVIEW & SUBMIT tab: Review the submission and click 'Submit'.
Troubleshooting: Contact biosamplehelp@ncbi.nlm.nih.gov for source metadata issues or sra@ncbi.nlm.nih.gov for raw sequence/metadata issues, including the submission ID (SUB#######).

steps.title: Retrieve Accessions
steps.instruction: Collect the generated accessions for BioSamples and SRA runs.

substeps.instruction: BioSample Accessions (SAMNxxxxxxxx): Available on the 'my submissions' page by clicking '## objects' or via the 'Download attributes file with BioSample accessions' link; also sent via email within 12 hours.
SRA Accessions (SRRxxxxxxx): Available on the 'My Submissions' page by clicking '## objects' or via the 'Download metadata file with SRA accession' link; also sent via email within 24 hours.

description: Important data stewardship and curation notes: Develop an internal method for storing and tracking your BioSample and SRR accessions! They are required for making future updates to your records. For updates, corrections, or retractions to your BioSample and SRA records, follow the guidance provided in the NCBI Curation Protocol. Some edits can be made within the submission portal and others need to be done via email. NCBI Bacterial Pathogen Data Curation Protocol: SOP for Editing GenomeTrakr Submissions by Ruth Timme Caution : It is possible for a single BioSample to have more than one SRR ID. Two scenarios include: Two runs were submitted for the same isolate/BioSample, which is not generally recommended for surveillance. Follow Step 3 in the NCBI curation protocol to retract one of them). if the initial submission was retracted and a new run was submitted. It's important to keep track of both IDs, even if one was retracted. Important data stewardship and curation notes: Develop an internal method for storing and tracking your BioProject accessions! They are required for every BioSample and sequence data submission to ensure proper linkage. Bookmark URLs for each of your data BioProjects to monitor the public-facing view of your submissions. e.g. Virginia DCLS's GenomeTrakr Salmonella BP: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/bioproject/219491 For updates to your BioProjects, follow the guidance provided in the NCBI Curation Protocol. Some edits can be made within the submission portal and others need to be done via email. go to step #2.14 NCBI Data Curation Protocol. **Pre-Submission Metadata Template Validation** Validate your sample and SRA metadata prior to uploading to NCBI using the following protocol: Guidance for populating and validating GenomeTrakr metadata templates (BioSample and SRA) by Ruth Timme
